Based on my search, I can provide you with information about **Medi-Cal**:

## What is Medi-Cal?

**Medi-Cal** is California's Medicaid program — a public health insurance program that provides free or low-cost medical services to eligible California residents. It is administered by the California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS).

## Key Features

- **Coverage**: Includes doctor visits, hospital care, prescription drugs, preventive services, mental health care, dental services (through Denti-Cal), vision care, and more
- **Eligibility**: Based on income, family size, age, disability status, and other factors
- **Expansion**: Under the Affordable Care Act, California expanded Medi-Cal to cover more low-income adults without dependent children

## Who Qualifies?

Eligibility categories include:
- Low-income families with children
- Pregnant women
- Seniors (65+)
- Persons with disabilities
- Children in foster care
- Former foster youth up to age 26
- Low-income adults (19-64) under the expansion

## How to Apply

- **Online**: Through [Covered California](https://www.coveredca.com) or [BenefitsCal](https://www.benefitscal.com)
- **Phone**: Contact your county social services office
- **In-person**: At county human services agencies

## Recent Developments

California has been working on expanding Medi-Cal coverage, including to undocumented immigrants of all ages (full expansion completed in 2024), and has eliminated most asset limits for certain eligibility categories.
